sources.entry: Lemmy - Link aggregator for the fediverse (alternative to Reddit). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Rust
Lemmy | Federated link aggregator and forum, a Reddit alternative

summary.one_liner: Lemmy is a self-hostable, federated link aggregator and forum for the fediverse, positioned as an alternative to Reddit.
summary.what_it_does: Lemmy lets users subscribe to forums (communities), post links, text or images, and vote and comment on them, similar to Reddit, Lobste.rs or Hacker News. Servers are federated, so a user registered on one server can subscribe to communities and discuss with users on other servers. Each server sets its own moderation policy, with site admins and community moderators who can sticky, lock, remove and restore posts and comments, ban users, and keep public moderation logs. Other listed features include private messaging, notifications (optionally by email), RSS/Atom feeds, cross-posting, similar-post search, NSFW tagging, and full data erasure. The server is written in Rust and the README says it supports arm64 and Raspberry Pi, with Docker and Ansible deployment options.
use_cases: Run a private or community-specific Reddit-style forum
Join decentralized link aggregation across the fediverse
Host a federated discussion board for a group
Run link and discussion communities without corporate control
Deploy a self-hosted forum on a Raspberry Pi or arm64 server
Moderate communities with admin and moderator tools
how_to_run: Read the Lemmy Administration Docs (linked from the README) for installation
Docker and Ansible deployment options are mentioned in the README
For development: see Contributing instructions, Docker Development, and Local Development docs
notable: Federated design: servers interoperate across the fediverse, like email
Full vote scores and live-updating comment threads
Public moderation logs and multi-level moderation roles
caveats: Installation details are in external administration docs, not the README itself
Federation means content and users span other servers outside your control
